limits: Input and root Interaction are descriptor helpers, not device polling, held-state management, dispatch or action-to-target wiring. Action-map object values are discarded; duplicate IDs overwrite. Several descriptor numeric fields permit nonfinite values until a stricter downstream boundary.

Queue fulfill selects by ID or first subject match before requiring open status; an earlier terminal entry can block a later open request for the same subject. Arbitrary initial statuses are accepted; counters are not derived from terminal input state. Time advances only when called.

Fulfillment complete checks ID/open status and nonnegative reward only, not arrival, proximity or deadline; expiry requires advance. nearestOpen ignores each request's own radius. Reward is caller-overridable.

Transfer advance reuses cached positions when updates omitted. Direct transfer trusts supplied dwell and does not clear active transfer state. New operation IDs can repeat a completed subject; operation-id idempotency is not once-per-subject delivery.

Assistance attach does not enforce attachDistance or carrier existence, and attachment does not move targets. Completion requires neither attachment nor a destination. Stable/attached status can disagree with urgency/attachedTo; loss has no dedicated emitted event.
Affordance nearby honors both radii, but activate does not check proximity or allowed action. Completion emits a descriptor event; game objective/world effects remain caller-owned.
Fulfillment, assistance and affordance lastEvent objects patched by services are replaced by the generic base 'updated' marker.

Transport adapter matches open requests by callId or riderId, not arrival stop. It captures the open list once; multiple arrivals may target the same request. A partial retry may fail before reaching child-operation deduplication because the fulfilled request is no longer open.

Adapters mutate child domains before committing a parent receipt; later failure leaves earlier child mutations. No atomic whole-workflow rollback is implemented here. Economy adapter accepts effect-shaped outcomes without checking receipt origin or restricting to approved terminal outcome kinds.

Inspected tests cover selected descriptors, deadline/dwell/capacity cases, clone isolation and sequential happy-path replay. Six recipe checks prove dependency selection only. No device execution, whole-game loop, stale-position, concurrent/partial failure, or coordinated reset proof.

State writes can reach engine/world objects without an allowlist or atomic batch. Default event timestamps use Date.now and module-global event sequence numbers, so full snapshots are not solely driven by supplied simulation time.

Broadcast iteration can deliver one event to a newly started successor. Cancelling children notifies their still-active parent before marking it cancelled, allowing completion/start side effects; parent failure does not consistently terminate descendants. Manual dispatch is not scoped by metadata node ID.

Public frame-driver bind methods are no-ops, but Engine.tick does drive frame progression. Additional lifecycle surface binding can duplicate frame delivery; other surface bridges dispatch specific and generic events.

No full reset/loadSnapshot contract; asynchronous callbacks, cancellation, queue bounds and reentrant delivery remain unguarded. Five tests cover successful fixture paths, not cancellation/restart recovery or a playable scene.
compute: Graph validation checks declared references and cycles, not inferred data hazards, binding sizes, kernel ports or provider language support. supports() declarations do not prove execution compatibility.

Positive finite mass/principal inertia can be tiny enough that reciprocal derivation returns Infinity without a final finite-output check. Very large finite quaternion components can overflow the norm and normalize to zero components. Direct normalization/inspection can therefore succeed on outputs that fail later portable/re-normalization checks.

Body replacement/transition revision guards protect that record only. Removal/redefinition does not retain a lifetime generation, so revision 1 may recur under a reused ID. Snapshot checks do not enforce bodyRevision >= sum of record revisions or sequence consistency like Collider does. nextRecord uses default normalizers rather than installed body-state parts.

Finite coefficient inputs can overflow average/multiply/geometric-mean results; no final finite-output check on pair resolution. Anisotropy selects one material direction and coefficients rather than combining directions or transforming them into contact coordinates; density is not used to calculate body mass.

Compound/scaled references are text-only at registry define/load: no child existence, recursive cycle/depth, or removal dependency check. Collider validates only the top-level shape ID, not its nested graph. Referenced shapes can be removed or redefined independently.

Convex accepts >=4 unique vertices without noncoplanarity/hull construction. Triangle-mesh checks indices but not repeated indices per triangle, zero area, manifoldness or winding; duplicated positions are rejected even when an indexed asset could legitimately use them. No aggregate vertex/triangle/heightfield/compound-size budget.

Plane normal is normalized while offset is retained unchanged; adapter must define offset convention explicitly. Capsules with zero half-height are rejected; positive nonuniform scaled shapes are accepted as descriptors regardless of backend support. No capability negotiation or provider-specific cooking validation.

Collider dependency checks run on define/replace/load, not on reads or lifecycle transition. Body revision updates/removal and shape/material removal can invalidate existing collider records without notification. groupId and excludedColliderIds are metadata; no group registry/existence resolution here. Sensors/triggers only select behavior fields; no overlap events or gameplay effects. Missing lifecycle-command status defaults enabled, so omission can reenable a collider.
